name: Short-Form Project, Asset, And Template System
use_when: A creator, client, or agent will produce multiple Reels, Shorts, TikToks, ads, or YouTube clips over time.
The edit depends on reusable overlays, SFX, music, fonts, backgrounds, icons, and render versions.
The agent needs a clean handoff between raw media, assets, Premiere, After Effects, and final exports.
avoid_when: The request is a one-off technical trim with no reusable style or client system.
The user has an existing folder/project convention that must be followed instead.
The setup work would delay an urgent small delivery more than it helps.

timeline_pattern.pattern: root_folders -> per_project_folder -> raw_media_images_renders -> nle_project_by_client_or_channel -> template_bins -> reusable_timeline_assets -> per_reel_sequence
timeline_pattern.root_rule: Separate personal/channel projects, client projects, and shared editing assets.
timeline_pattern.per_reel_rule: Create a folder per reel with raw clips/audio, images/assets, and renders/exports.
timeline_pattern.template_rule: Keep reusable overlays, SFX, and music in template bins or template timelines so finishing passes are drag-and-drop rather than search-heavy.
timeline_pattern.naming_rule: Name projects, bins, sequences, and renders by client/channel, output type, reel number, and short description.

motion.rule: Store reusable motion assets by job, such as overlay, texture, hook text, background, or transition.

sound.rule: Organize SFX by job, such as whoosh, hit, typewriter, camera, riser, reward, music, or ambience.

captions.rule: Store caption styles by brand/client and do not mix caption presets across brands without review.

color.rule: Store brand colors, gradient/background samples, and approved looks with the style/template files.

implementation.ffmpeg: Store render names, source paths, output paths, and target specs in project metadata so ffmpeg conforms and QC scripts can find the right files.
implementation.remotion: Create a project config with brandId, outputType, assetFolders, styleTokens, sequences, renderTargets, and reusable component IDs.
implementation.blender: Keep reusable 3D assets, cameras, fonts, and renders in project folders separated from raw media.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Keep a folder of reusable brand overlays, SFX, fonts, captions, and exports; duplicate project templates for each new reel.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use one Premiere project per client/channel and output type when batching; create bins for each reel plus template bins/timelines for overlays, SFX, music, and common assets.

common_mistakes: Creating a new NLE project for every reel when a client/channel template would speed repeated work.
Downloading huge asset packs all at once and losing the few assets needed for the current style.
Saving renders beside raw assets with vague names.
Mixing client assets, personal brand assets, and shared assets without clear folder boundaries.
Using a reusable preset without knowing which brand or project it belongs to.
qc: Does the reel folder contain separate raw media, images/assets, and renders/exports?
Are reusable overlays, SFX, music, and caption styles in template bins or folders?
Can another agent identify the final sequence and latest render by filename?
Are client/channel style assets separated from generic shared assets?
Does every external asset have a source/license note when it is used in a project?
